## Related AI guides [...] ## AgentGrid.io FAQs

### Who makes AgentGrid.io?

AgentGrid.io is a product of Anima App, Inc., and purchases continue through Anima.

### Do agents count as paid seats?

No. AgentGrid says every plan includes unlimited agent seats, and billing is per team covering all of that team's workspaces.

### How do I add work to AgentGrid?

You ask your agent to share an artifact on AgentGrid.io once it is ready, or drop a file or folder onto the site to start.

## AgentGrid.io Alternatives

Popular alternatives to AgentGrid.io include Voilà, Hiding AI and Loopa. Compare their pricing and what each is best for below. [...] Use cases listed on the site include publishing websites, sharing AI-generated work, shared working memory, and working alongside Obsidian, Claude Design and ChatGPT.

Pricing: a Free plan includes 100 artifacts, 1 workspace, unlimited agent seats and web publishing. Paid plans include Lite at USD 9 a month, Pro at USD 50 a month and Business from USD 180 a month, with more artifacts and workspaces, custom domains, roles and permissions and SSO.

It is suited to teams that use several AI agents and want one source of truth for the documents, apps and designs those agents produce.

results.title: Claude Docs: What is Claude Docs, Pros, Cons, and Alternatives — AgentGrid
results.content:
Notion AI adds an on-demand Notion Agent, Custom Agents for recurring workflows, Enterprise Search across connected apps, AI Meeting Notes, and in-page writing help. This makes Notion broader than Claude Docs: it is less a focused writing canvas and more a workspace with documents at its center.

Choose it when: the document must connect to structured knowledge, project status, databases, and repeatable workflows.

Watch for: the flexibility can add setup and workspace complexity. If your goal is simply “turn this Claude conversation into a polished doc,” Claude Docs is more direct. If you need external agents to share one versioned artifact, AgentGrid.io is more purpose-built.

## The verdict: should you use Claude Docs? [...] The result is closer to an AI-native Google Doc, similarly to AgentGrid.io. The document has its own place in the Artifacts tab, can contain multiple tabs, and can use context from your files, memory, projects, skills, and connected apps.

 Claude Docs interface showing a shared document, chart, comments, and the Claude conversation 

Claude Docs combines a conversation, editable document, visual data, and collaborator comments in one interface. Product image: Anthropic, published by The Verge.

 

Availability and price

Anthropic currently lists Claude Docs as a beta for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans.

For ChatGPT, free Claude users, and other agents, AgentGrid.io is the natural alternative as a collaborative document editor for humans and agents. [...] ### Does Claude Docs have version history?

Not yet. Anthropic lists version history as a known beta limitation. If restorable, attributed revisions are important, AgentGrid.io or an established office editor may be a better place for the durable copy.

### Can I export a Claude Doc?

Yes. Current export options are Microsoft Word, PDF, Markdown, and Google Docs.

### Can clients open a Claude Doc without a Claude account?

No. Shared Claude Docs require a Claude account. Team and Enterprise Docs also cannot yet be shared outside the organization.

### What is the best Claude Docs alternative?

Choose AgentGrid.io for cross-agent artifacts and version history, Google Docs for familiar office collaboration, and Notion for connected docs, wikis, projects, databases, and workspace AI.
